body:
**What you must know:** the page itself was the problem, not the agent. An agent's write did reach the board, but your open page only showed what its live feed told it, and a feed that died or missed a write was never retried. The fix is on main: each feed reconnects, and every 15 s the page asks for what was written since its last read (a quiet tick costs a few bytes), with a full re-read whenever you come back to the page. **You will only see it after the orchestrator republishes your board page** (O54 does it after this Done). That delay is itself the most repeated problem in the list below (row 2).

## A. Why you had to close and reopen (measured)

**What the rows show.** Your comment `wczwg8ugmmwufo0o9wn0` under CL34 was saved at 01:21:56. O54's reply `o54-docs-in-posts-0130` carries `arrived_at` 01:24:55. Only your own open page writes `arrived_at` (`stampArrivals`, `kit/board/board.template.html:1478`, when you are the owner), and it writes it the first time that page sees the comment. The CL35 prompt was committed at 01:27:19, after your chat question. So your page first saw O54's reply at 01:24:55: when you reopened, not when O54 wrote it. (O54 also stamped its reply `created_at` 01:30:00, five minutes ahead of the real time. That is row 14 below.)

**How the page listens** (`kit/board/board.template.html`, before this fix): it opens one live feed (`onSnapshot`) for posts, one for comments and one for typing, at lines 3584, 3588 and 3600. Attached boards (`repos/<id>/...`) go through `kit/claude/artifact_repos.js:81`, which opens the same feed on `repos/<id>/comments`. Nothing else ever re-reads the board.
- **Cause 1 (kit):** the comments feed's error handler was `function () {}` (old line 3604), and so was the typing feed's. The platform's db contract says a feed is ended for good with `unavailable` "when the page's host itself stops answering" (a phone that slept, an app in the background), and that "a fresh onSnapshot is the only recovery". The page never opened a new one, so comments stopped arriving and nothing said so. The posts feed did show "The board stopped updating. Reload to reconnect", but only in the small status line.
- **Cause 2 (platform or kit, not settled):** a write the realtime stream does not deliver was never shown. The contract promises other viewers' writes live, or at least through a ~30 s refresh. An ArtifactData write from a session is made as **you** (the same user as the page). I cannot open your claude.ai page from here, so I could not measure whether the stream skips a write made by the same user from another client. Either way, the kit now re-reads by itself.

**Measured** on the real Artifact page built from this repo (Chromium, the stub db of `kit/claude/test_artifact_live.js`, page open on a post of the attached board):
| case | page before | page after |
|---|---|---|
| the stream delivers the write | shown in 12 ms | shown in 7 ms |
| the stream never delivers it | never shown (8 s) | shown in 0.25 s |
| the comments feed ends with `unavailable`, then a write | never shown (8 s) | shown in 1.8 s |
| **your case on your data**: the 56 posts and 112 comments of this board from the live Artifact, CL34 open, O54's real reply written from outside with the stream silent | never shown (8 s) | shown in 2.8 s |
(The test checks every 3 s; the real page does it every 15 s, and reads everything at once when you come back to the page.)

**Rendering is not the cause:** when the stream delivers, a reply stamped 5 minutes in the future shows under its parent in 7 to 12 ms.

## A. The fix
In `kit/board/board.template.html`, `liveQuery` (the CL35 block before `/* Boot */`):
1. **Each feed reconnects.** After a terminal error (any code except `revoked` or `invalid_argument`), it opens a fresh `onSnapshot` after 2, 4, 8 s and so on, up to 60 s. The posts status says "Reconnecting to the board..." meanwhile.
2. **Every 15 s, while the page is visible, it asks only for what is new:** comments with `created_at` after its last read, and posts with `updated_at` or `created_at` after it. The last read's time is the page's own clock, less a margin: 10 minutes for comments (agents write their times by hand, ahead or behind), 1 minute for posts (the kit's tools stamp `updated_at`). What comes back is merged by id, and nothing is redrawn when nothing changed.
3. **A full re-read** happens when you come back to the page (`visibilitychange`, `focus`, `pageshow`) and after a feed died. That full read also catches deletions, and edits to older comments.
- It applies to posts, comments and typing, on the primary board and on attached boards, because `artifact_repos.js`'s queries follow the board you picked.
- **Cost, measured** on this board's real data (56 posts, 112 comments) in the test's byte counter: a full read is 282,804 bytes; a quiet 15 s tick is 8 bytes. Before the narrowing (O54's review), every tick was a full read. On Harmonize's board the comments alone are 1,391,105 bytes (1,381 comments), so that first version cost about 330 MB an hour per open tab. A tick now costs only what was written in the margin.
- **Bursts and the default test** (O54's second check): the comment poll reads by `created_at`, 100 a page, until a page comes back short. The default suite now checks a silent burst of 150 comments (all shown in 0.8 s; it fails without the paging) and a quiet tick against a full read (8 bytes vs 61,211 with 300 older comments).
- **Limit:** a comment an agent stamps more than 10 minutes behind the real time shows only at the next full read (when you come back to the page). Row 14's fix (the kit stamps the time) removes that case.
- **Test:** `kit/claude/test_artifact_live.js` (the three cases above, plus `KIT_LIVE_DATA=.kit/run/artifact/base` for your case on your data) runs in `tests/test_artifact_cross_repo.py` (PageSwitcher). It fails on the page from before the fix.

## B. Everything that has gone wrong with using the kit
One row per problem, deduplicated: **62 rows, 31 fixed (row 1 waiting for the republish), 16 worked around, 15 open.** "Seen by": you, or the session that reported it. Rows marked pre-kit predate the kit. Folded together: O54's clerk rows went into 6 (ignored), 9 (Where this began), 16 (memory files), 18 (trunk_push), 22 (seeded clones), 27 and 28 (access), 31 (launcher) and 32. ## Next kit parts proposed (no launch)
Ordered by how often each one cost you something.
1. **Republish on merge** (row 2): when a merge to main changes the page (`kit/board/*.html`, `shim.js`, `kit/claude/artifact_*.js`), `end_session.py` runs `update_board.py` and hands the orchestrator one publish line. **Do it first, so this CL35 fix reaches you.**
2. **An agent's answer always lands on the board** (rows 62, 5): a reply goes through `board_cli.py reply` on `repos/<id>/comments` (K6) and never through ArtifactComments; the second check mark appears only when the answering session marks the comment read.
3. **The clock comes from the kit** (rows 14, 4): `board_cli.py` and the ArtifactData batches the kit prints stamp `created_at` themselves; a hand-written time is refused.
4. **Launch and pull that do not miss** (rows 60, 61, 59): `kit.py launch` fetches the part branch before pushing; a delta `artifact pull` also gets each post the train names; a part branch runs the kit of main.
5. **Docs in posts** (row 20): O54's proposal under CL34.
6. **The kit's small breakages** (rows 54, 46, 48, 43): the TaskCreate/TaskUpdate hook, `next-clerk.py`, the HL1 train row, `files-sent`'s wholesale index.
7. **Crashed parts continue** (row 15): CL17, still planned.
8. **Harmonize access for parts** (row 27): an environment or repo grant so parts run `real_project` themselves.
9. **A real device run** (row 29): your phone on the republished page, once per page change.

title: Why the owner doesn't see agents' board writes until he reopens, and one list of what went wrong with the kit
verdict: Your open page only showed what its live feed told it: a feed that died or missed an agent's write was never retried (kit, not the agent). Fixed on main: feeds reconnect, the page asks for new writes every 15 s; needs a republish.
